scenario.name: Microsoft SQL Server Security & Mandiant DFIR — MSSQL xp_cmdshell / Ole Automation Reconfiguration (EventID 15457) & sqlservr.exe Forensics
scenario.overview: A vault bookkeeper is supposed to only file and fetch account ledgers, never operate the building workshop. Investigators trace an intrusion where a privileged caller unlocks the bookkeeper hidden workshop switch, loads two helper toolkits to run floor commands, and installs a permanent custom stamp inside the vault catalog. In this scenario (T1059.003, Microsoft SQL Server Security & Mandiant DFIR, MSSQL xp_cmdshell / Ole Automation Reconfiguration , EventID 15457 & sqlservr.exe Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: sp_configure Reconfiguration of show, then xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load, then cLR Stored Procedure Persistence. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering sp_configure Reconfiguration of show, then xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load, then CLR Stored Procedure Persistence, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: sp_configure Reconfiguration of show advanced options & xp_cmdshell (Application EventID 15457)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059.003 - MSSQL sp_configure Option Reconfiguration)
stages.description: First, investigators inspect the vault configuration book and see two safety locks flipped open in rapid succession: one exposing hidden settings and a second enabling the direct workshop command lever. Because xp_cmdshell and Ole Automation Procedures are disabled by default (value 0), the attacker executes sp_configure "show advanced options", 1; RECONFIGURE; followed by sp_configure "xp_cmdshell", 1; RECONFIGURE;. SQL Server immediately writes EventID 15457 (Source: MSSQLSERVER) to the Windows Application Event Log and the SQL Server ERRORLOG ("Configuration option 'xp_cmdshell' changed from 0 to 1") (logged in WinEvent Event 15457 with LogChannel=Application , Source: MSSQLSERVER & SQL ERRORLOG, EventID=15457 , Configuration Option Changed, ConfigurationOption=xp_cmdshell , 0 -> 1 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes T-SQL: EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE; (which executes privileged T-SQL stored procedures , sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE; followed by xp_cmdshell or sp_OACreate 'WScript.Shell' in so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "sp_configure Reconfiguration of show advanced options & xp_cmdshell , Application EventID 15457" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact Application EventID 15457 (MSSQLSERVER): Configuration option 'xp_cmdshell' changed from 0 to 1. runs (which executes privileged T-SQL stored procedures , sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE; followed by xp_cmdshell or sp_OACreate 'WScript.Shell' in so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "sp_configure Reconfiguration of show advanced options & xp_cmdshell , Application EventID 15457" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ MSSQLSERVER EventID 15457: Configuration option xp_cmdshell changed from 0 to 1 / ⇠#1 ACK 15457) from Node ① (#1 TDS Client (:1433 SQL)) to Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll).

stages.title: Stage 2: xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load & sqlservr.exe Child Shell Execution (Sysmon EventID 1 & 7)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059.003 - sqlservr.exe -> cmd.exe Parent-Child Anomaly)
stages.description: Moments later, the bookkeeper pulls two specialized hardware libraries off the shelf, one built for shell commands and another for external automation objects, and immediately spawns an office command console directly beneath the ledger desk. When the attacker invokes EXEC master..xp_cmdshell (or sp_OACreate "WScript.Shell"), sqlservr.exe loads C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL16.MSSQLSERVER\MSSQL\Binn\xplog70.dll (or odsole70.dll, Sysmon EventID 7) and spawns cmd.exe /c ... under the SQL Server service account (NT Service\MSSQLSERVER, Sysmon EventID 1) (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate + 7 , ImageLoaded xplog70.dll, ParentImage=sqlservr.exe, ChildImage=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe, ServiceAccount=NT SERVICE\MSSQLSERVER , Holds SeImpersonatePrivilege so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 7: Image=sqlservr.exe ImageLoaded=...\MSSQL\Binn\xplog70.dll (or odsole70.dll) (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , Sysmon EventID 7: Image=sqlservr.exe ImageLoaded=...\MSSQL\Binn\xplog70.dll so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load & sqlservr.exe Child Shell Execution , Sysmon EventID 1 & 7" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\...\sqlservr.exe -> Image=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\...\sqlser so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load & sqlservr.exe Child Shell Execution , Sysmon EventID 1 & 7" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ cmd.exe /c "whoami /all & net group "Domain Admins" /domain" / ⇠#2 ACK 1) from Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Tabular Data Stream (TDS)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll).

stages.title: Stage 3: CLR Stored Procedure Persistence (sys.assemblies) & Default Trace (.trc) Forensics
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1505.001 - Server Software Component: SQL Stored Procedures)
stages.description: To maintain quiet access even if the workshop lever is locked again, the intruder registers an unsigned custom extension right inside the vault catalog while leaving a clear audit trail inside the automatic rolling trace reel. Even if the attacker sets xp_cmdshell back to 0 (generating another EventID 15457 from 1 to 0) and registers a malicious .NET CLR assembly via CREATE ASSEMBLY ... Next, the follow-up artifact Default Trace Query: SELECT TextData, LoginName, HostName, StartTime FROM sys.fn_trace_gettable('C:\...\log.trc', DEFAULT); runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , Default Trace Query: SELECT TextData, LoginName, HostName, StartTime FROM sys. so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1505.001 during "CLR Stored Procedure Persistence , sys.assemblies & Default Trace .trc Forensics" under the database daemon's service account). steps.plainTitle: CLR Stored Procedure Persistence (sys.assemblies) & Default Trace (.trc) Forensics
steps.storyAnalogy: To maintain quiet access even if the workshop lever is locked again, the intruder registers an unsigned custom extension right inside the vault catalog while leaving a clear audit trail inside the automatic rolling trace reel.
steps.simpleExplanation: Even if the attacker sets xp_cmdshell back to 0 (generating another EventID 15457 from 1 to 0) and registers a malicious .NET CLR assembly via CREATE ASSEMBLY ... WITH PERMISSION_SET = UNSAFE, SQL Server’s built-in Default Trace (C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\...\MSSQL\Log\log_*.trc) and sys.assemblies / sys.assembly_files catalog views preserve the exact DDL timestamp, login name, client hostname, and raw PE bytes of the assembly (logged in WinEvent Event 15457 with ForensicArtifact=SQL Server Default Trace , MSSQL\Log\log_*.trc & sys.assembly_files, PersistenceMechanism=User-Defined CLR Assembly , PERMISSION_SET = UNSAFE, RecoverableBinary=SELECT content FROM sys.assembly_files , Starts with 0x4D5A MZ header so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes T-SQL Forensics: SELECT name, permission_set_desc, create_date FROM sys.assemblies WHERE is_user_defined = 1; (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , T-SQL Forensics: SELECT name, permission_set_desc, create_date FROM sys.assemb so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1505.001 during "CLR Stored Procedure Persistence , sys.assemblies & Default Trace .trc Forensics" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact Default Trace Query: SELECT TextData, LoginName, HostName, StartTime FROM sys.fn_trace_gettable('C:\...\log.trc', DEFAULT); runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , Default Trace Query: SELECT TextData, LoginName, HostName, StartTime FROM sys. so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1505.001 during "CLR Stored Procedure Persistence , sys.assemblies & Default Trace .trc Forensics" under the database daemon's service account).
